notes: Continuation of a handwritten letter signed R. Hartshorne. The writer qualifies his opening claim with ‘I believe’ and says the artinian hypothesis in the proposition on p. 38 is unnecessary under the stated AR-J-adic noetherian hypotheses. He gives three exact sequences, invokes inverse limit and Artin–Rees, and claims that the middle system is AR-J-adic. These are the writer's claims, not a proof verified in this reading. Three pale arrows cross the intervening text from the bottom sequence to X, Y and Z; their hand is not established. The closing paragraph names the paper ‘Affine Duality and Cofiniteness’ and promises a copy when ready. The one-word deletion remains unreadable. The marginal pair remains an uncertain colon. No date or salutation occurs on this leaf. One manuscript page number, 2, appears at top; archive number 54 is at bottom left and is recorded only in a comment. The letter has no separate title; its paper title is quoted in the prose. The author draws no explicit question mark here. H supplies description only, so h_reading is null and diff_h is false throughout; its unrelated trailing cover note was disregarded. No substantive C difference was found; all four explicit C doubts were independently inspected and retained. The raised AR and its hyphen, lower-case let, all primes, alphabets, signs, quote pairs, arrows and punctuation were checked. The pale irregular contour at the left edge of the middle region was assessed as paper staining, not a textual or diagrammatic mark.
math_reading_decisions: The short terminal downstrokes joined to the plus signs before Y and Z remain ambiguous between n+1 and n+; the shared ambiguity is marked at its first occurrence only.
Read the limit shaft from its visible left-facing head.
Read one and two primes directly and distinguish the doubled A used for the defined projective system from the plain quotient numerator A.
Read the final arrow label as two waves over a right-pointing arrow; keep P with lower capitals AR.
The three long pale upward strokes are connecting arrows between the bottom and top sequences, not deletion strokes.
No mathematical proof, computation or external background check was performed.
